comparisons.peer_topic: R&D Expense Increase and AI Headcount
comparisons.peer_summary: AMD's research and development expenses increased by 10% to $6.5 billion in 2024, primarily driven by higher employee-related costs resulting from an increase in headcount to support the company's AI strategy.
comparisons.comparison: Both MU and AMD report a 10% increase in R&D expenses for fiscal year 2024 compared to the prior year. However, the primary drivers differ: MU attributes the increase to higher employee compensation and higher volumes of development and prequalification wafers, noting that R&D varies with wafer processing and personnel costs. In contrast, AMD attributes its 10% increase specifically to higher employee-related costs resulting from increased headcount to support its AI strategy, without mentioning wafer volume impacts.

comparisons.comparison: Both companies discuss R&D expense increases driven by headcount and compensation. AVGO reports a much larger increase (77%) driven by higher compensation and headcount from the VMware Merger, along with higher stock-based compensation. MU reports a 10% increase driven by employee compensation and development wafer volumes. While both cite compensation/headcount as key drivers, AVGO's increase is heavily influenced by acquisition integration and stock-based compensation nuances, whereas MU's is tied to operational wafer processing volumes and personnel.
